original_claim: $36M median nuclear verdict for broker negligent-hiring
verified_value: $36M is the median nuclear verdict (jury awards > $10M) in trucking cases generally (carrier-facing) for 2022, per ATRI's December 2025 litigation update. The ILR May 2024 study puts the overall cross-category median at $21M and the product-liability peak at $36M in 2022. No actual broker-specific negligent-hiring nuclear verdicts exist in the record — broker negligent-hiring FAAAA preemption defense was available until Montgomery v. Caribe (May 14, 2026), meaning the broker-facing verdict pool is effectively zero cases. The $36M figure is a legitimate proxy for forward exposure (trucking cases with negligent-hiring factor increase expected awards 272.3%), but it must not be described as the 'broker negligent-hiring' median. It is the broader trucking industry median, applied as an exposure ceiling proxy.
precision_problem: The claim conflates two datasets: (1) ATRI's trucking carrier verdict median ($36M for 2022 trucking cases) and (2) ILR's product-liability case median ($36M peak in 2022). Neither data set is broker-specific. The FreightWaves 'Freight Broker Insurance Gap' article used $36M as a hypothetical broker-scenario number, not a measured broker verdict. The BeInsure article attributed it to ATRI but also in the context of trucking generally.

supporting_sources.title: Nuclear Verdicts: An Update on Trends, Causes, and Solutions
supporting_sources.key_data: Overall median nuclear verdict 2013-2022: $21M. Auto accident median: $21M. Product liability median: $25M (peaked at $36M in 2022). ~1 in 4 auto accident nuclear verdicts involves a commercial trucking company. No broker-negligent-hiring category.
supporting_sources.note: The $36M in ILR is product-liability peak (2022), not trucking specifically.

supporting_sources.title: The Freight Broker Insurance Gap Is Now Real
supporting_sources.key_data: Cites $36M as trucking median per ATRI December 2025. Uses it as hypothetical broker exposure, explicitly noting 'the $36 million judgment a jury just handed down because the broker put a load on a carrier with a conditional safety rating' is a hypothetical example, not an actual broker verdict. Confirms no actual broker-facing negligent-hiring nuclear verdicts on record.

supporting_sources.title: Freight Brokers Face New Insurance Gap After Supreme Court Ruling
supporting_sources.key_data: Attributes $36M to ATRI December 2025 trucking litigation update; applies it to broker exposure context. Does not claim $36M is a broker-specific figure. Confirms ATRI defines 'nuclear verdict' as >$10M.

supporting_sources.title: ATRI Report: Trucking Nuclear Verdicts and Litigation Costs Surge
supporting_sources.date: December 2025 (article reporting on the ATRI release)
supporting_sources.key_data: ATRI December 2025: tractor-trailer tort case filings grew 3.7% annually 2014-2023; median nuclear verdict $36M in 2022 (~50% higher than 2013 median); verdicts >$50M rose 6.4 percentage points. Negligent hiring/onboarding increases expected award by 272.3%.

supporting_sources.title: Supreme Court Holds Negligent Selection Claims Against Brokers Are Not Preempted
supporting_sources.key_data: Montgomery v. Caribe analysis. Confirms no verdict data for broker negligent-hiring cases cited — Scopelitis discusses legal exposure but provides no verdict-size benchmark, corroborating that broker-specific verdict data does not yet exist.

recommendation: Replace the claim 'Median nuclear verdict in trucking negligent-hiring cases (now relevant to brokers post-Montgomery): $36M' with: 'Median nuclear verdict in trucking cases reached $36M in 2022 (ATRI, December 2025) — a 50% increase over the 2013 median of ~$24M. No broker-specific negligent-hiring verdict data exists yet (FAAAA preemption blocked such claims pre-Montgomery); however, ATRI data shows that negligent hiring/onboarding as an aggravating factor increases expected verdict awards by 272.3%, making trucking-industry medians the best available forward-looking exposure proxy for brokers post-Montgomery. The $36M figure should be cited as the trucking-industry median, not a broker-specific median. [Source: ATRI Nuclear Verdicts and Litigation Cost Update, December 2025; ILR Nuclear Verdicts: An Update, May 2024 (PDF)]'
